docs.title: ladle
docs.text: ladle is a Python library providing fast, ergonomic bindings to the noodles bioinformatics I/O library, built with PyO3. It also includes a parallel genomic interval engine backed by Rayon with zero-copy Apache Arrow output.

docs.title: What ladle gives you
docs.text:
• Read and write BAM, SAM, VCF, BCF, FASTQ, BGZF — sequential and random-access (indexed) readers
  • Columnar batch export — every reader can produce an Arrow RecordBatch consumable by Polars, Pandas, or PyArrow directly
  • Genomic interval operations — overlap, nearest, count, merge, cluster, coverage, and more, all parallelised with Rayon
  • Zero-copy data exchange — Arrow C Data Interface throughout; no serialisation overhead

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install ladle

# Optional DataFrame extras
pip install "ladle[arrow]"   # pyarrow
pip install "ladle[polars]"  # polars
pip install "ladle[pandas]"  # pandas

Note

ladle is not yet on PyPI — see Quick start for building from source.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.11+
  • Rust 1.88+ (for building from source)

docs.title: Install from source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/WindowGenerator/ladle.git
cd ladle

# Create a virtual environment
python3.11 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

# Install build tool and runtime dependencies
pip install maturin pyarrow polars pandas pytest

# Build both Rust extensions and install in develop mode
VIRTUAL_ENV="$(pwd)/.venv" maturin develop --manifest-path ladle-io/Cargo.toml
VIRTUAL_ENV="$(pwd)/.venv" maturin develop --manifest-path ladle-ops/Cargo.toml

Or with just:

just build

docs.title: Verify the install
docs.text:
import ladle.io.bam as bam
import ladle.io.vcf as vcf
import ladle.ops.intervals as intervals

print(bam.Reader)         # <class 'ladle.io.bam.Reader'>
print(intervals.overlap)  # <built-in function overlap>

docs.title: Read a BAM file
docs.text:
from ladle.io.bam import Reader

with Reader.from_path("sample.bam") as r:
    header = r.read_header()
    for record in r:
        print(record.name(), record.alignment_start())

docs.title: Load BAM into a Polars DataFrame
docs.text:
from ladle.io.bam import Reader

with Reader.from_path("sample.bam") as r:
    r.read_header()
    batch = r.records_to_batch()

df = batch.to_polars()
print(df.head())

docs.title: Find overlapping intervals
docs.text:
import polars as pl
import ladle.ops.intervals as intervals

a = pl.DataFrame({"chrom": ["chr1", "chr1"], "start": [0, 10], "end": [15, 25]})
b = pl.DataFrame({"chrom": ["chr1"], "start": [12], "end": [20]})

result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.overlap(a, b))
print(result)

docs.title: ladle.ops.intervals
docs.text: Genomic interval operations backed by a Rust engine (Rayon parallel, zero-copy Arrow I/O). All functions accept any of PyArrow, Polars, or Pandas DataFrames and return a pyarrow.RecordBatch.

docs.title: Column name requirements
docs.text:
Every input DataFrame must contain columns named:

Semantic Accepted column names Chromosome chrom, contig, chr Start (0-based) start, pos End (exclusive) end, stop

Rename before calling if your schema differs:

# Polars
df = df.rename({"seqname": "chrom", "chromStart": "start", "chromEnd": "end"})

# Pandas
df = df.rename(columns={"seqname": "chrom", "chromStart": "start", "chromEnd": "end"})

# PyArrow
batch = batch.rename_columns({"seqname": "chrom", "chromStart": "start", "chromEnd": "end"})

docs.title: overlap
docs.text:
Find all pairs of intervals from a and b that overlap.

Overlap condition: a.start < b.end and b.start < a.end (half-open intervals). Cross-chromosome pairs are never considered overlapping.

import polars as pl
import ladle.ops.intervals as intervals

a = pl.DataFrame({"chrom": ["chr1", "chr1"], "start": [1, 5], "end": [5, 10]})
b = pl.DataFrame({"chrom": ["chr1"], "start": [3], "end": [7]})

result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.overlap(a, b))
# shape: (2, 6)
# ┌──────────┬──────────┬────────┬──────────┬──────────┬────────┐
# │ a_chrom  ┆ a_start  ┆ a_end  ┆ b_chrom  ┆ b_start  ┆ b_end  │
# │ str      ┆ i64      ┆ i64    ┆ str      ┆ i64      ┆ i64    │
# ╞══════════╪══════════╪════════╪══════════╪══════════╪════════╡
# │ chr1     ┆ 1        ┆ 5      ┆ chr1     ┆ 3        ┆ 7      │
# │ chr1     ┆ 5        ┆ 10     ┆ chr1     ┆ 3        ┆ 7      │
# └──────────┴──────────┴────────┴──────────┴──────────┴────────┘

Use how="semi" to filter a to rows that have at least one overlap in b, without duplicating rows:

result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.overlap(a, b, how="semi"))
# Returns rows from a only; schema unchanged

docs.title: nearest
docs.text:
For each row in query, find the closest row in target on the same chromosome.

Distance is 0 for overlapping intervals, otherwise the number of bases between them. When no same-chromosome target exists, all b_* columns are null and distance is null.

query  = pl.DataFrame({"chrom": ["chr1", "chr2"], "start": [10, 50], "end": [20, 60]})
target = pl.DataFrame({"chrom": ["chr1", "chr1"], "start": [1, 30], "end": [8, 40]})

result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.nearest(query, target))
# ┌──────────┬──────────┬────────┬──────────┬──────────┬────────┬──────────┐
# │ a_chrom  ┆ a_start  ┆ a_end  ┆ b_chrom  ┆ b_start  ┆ b_end  ┆ distance │
# │ str      ┆ i64      ┆ i64    ┆ str      ┆ i64      ┆ i64    ┆ i64      │
# ╞══════════╪══════════╪════════╪══════════╪══════════╪════════╪══════════╡
# │ chr1     ┆ 10       ┆ 20     ┆ chr1     ┆ 30       ┆ 40     ┆ 11       │
# │ chr2     ┆ 50       ┆ 60     ┆ null     ┆ null     ┆ null   ┆ null     │
# └──────────┴──────────┴────────┴──────────┴──────────┴────────┴──────────┘

Use on_cols to group by additional key columns (e.g. sample ID) before finding the nearest:

result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.nearest(query, target, on_cols=["sample_id"]))

docs.title: count_overlaps
docs.text:
For each row in a, count how many rows in b overlap it. Returns all columns from a plus a count column (UInt32). Rows with no overlaps get count=0.

a = pl.DataFrame({"chrom": ["chr1", "chr1"], "start": [0, 5], "end": [10, 15]})
b = pl.DataFrame({"chrom": ["chr1", "chr1", "chr1"], "start": [1, 6, 12], "end": [4, 9, 20]})

result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.count_overlaps(a, b))
# ┌───────┬───────┬─────┬───────┐
# │ chrom ┆ start ┆ end ┆ count │
# │ str   ┆ i64   ┆ i64 ┆ u32   │
# ╞═══════╪═══════╪═════╪═══════╡
# │ chr1  ┆ 0     ┆ 10  ┆ 2     │
# │ chr1  ┆ 5     ┆ 15  ┆ 3     │
# └───────┴───────┴─────┴───────┘

docs.title: cluster
docs.text:
Assign a cluster_id to each interval. Overlapping or adjacent intervals on the same chromosome share the same ID (UInt32, 0-based). Returns all columns from a plus cluster_id.

a = pl.DataFrame({
    "chrom": ["chr1", "chr1", "chr1", "chr2"],
    "start": [0, 5, 20, 0],
    "end":   [10, 15, 30, 5],
})

result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.cluster(a))
# ┌───────┬───────┬─────┬────────────┐
# │ chrom ┆ start ┆ end ┆ cluster_id │
# │ str   ┆ i64   ┆ i64 ┆ u32        │
# ╞═══════╪═══════╪═════╪════════════╡
# │ chr1  ┆ 0     ┆ 10  ┆ 0          │
# │ chr1  ┆ 5     ┆ 15  ┆ 0          │
# │ chr1  ┆ 20    ┆ 30  ┆ 1          │
# │ chr2  ┆ 0     ┆ 5   ┆ 2          │
# └───────┴───────┴─────┴────────────┘

docs.title: merge
docs.text:
Merge overlapping intervals into non-overlapping spans. Returns only chrom/start/end columns (extra metadata columns are dropped).

a = pl.DataFrame({
    "chrom": ["chr1", "chr1", "chr1"],
    "start": [0, 5, 20],
    "end":   [10, 15, 30],
    "score": [1, 2, 3],   # dropped in output
})

result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.merge(a))
# ┌───────┬───────┬─────┐
# │ chrom ┆ start ┆ end │
# ╞═══════╪═══════╪═════╡
# │ chr1  ┆ 0     ┆ 15  │
# │ chr1  ┆ 20    ┆ 30  │
# └───────┴───────┴─────┘

docs.title: subtract
docs.text:
Return rows of a that have no overlap with any row in b. Entire rows are kept or dropped — no interval clipping. Schema is identical to a.

a = pl.DataFrame({"chrom": ["chr1", "chr1", "chr2"], "start": [0, 5, 0], "end": [5, 10, 5]})
b = pl.DataFrame({"chrom": ["chr1"], "start": [4], "end": [8]})

result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.subtract(a, b))
# Returns only the row chr2:0-5 (the two chr1 rows overlap b)

docs.title: complement
docs.text:
Return the gaps between intervals on each chromosome.

If chrom_sizes is provided, also emits leading gaps [0, first_start) and trailing gaps [last_end, chrom_size). Returns only chrom/start/end columns.

a = pl.DataFrame({
    "chrom": ["chr1", "chr1"],
    "start": [10, 50],
    "end":   [30, 70],
})

# Without chrom_sizes — only inter-interval gaps
result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.complement(a))
# ┌───────┬───────┬─────┐
# │ chrom ┆ start ┆ end │
# ╞═══════╪═══════╪═════╡
# │ chr1  ┆ 30    ┆ 50  │
# └───────┴───────┴─────┘

# With chrom_sizes — leading and trailing gaps included
result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.complement(a, chrom_sizes={"chr1": 100}))
# ┌───────┬───────┬─────┐
# │ chrom ┆ start ┆ end │
# ╞═══════╪═══════╪═════╡
# │ chr1  ┆ 0     ┆ 10  │
# │ chr1  ┆ 30    ┆ 50  │
# │ chr1  ┆ 70    ┆ 100 │
# └───────┴───────┴─────┘

docs.title: coverage
docs.text:
Compute per-base coverage depth as contiguous blocks. Returns chrom/start/end/depth (UInt32). Zero-depth regions are not emitted.

a = pl.DataFrame({
    "chrom": ["chr1", "chr1"],
    "start": [0, 5],
    "end":   [10, 15],
})

result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.coverage(a))
# ┌───────┬───────┬─────┬───────┐
# │ chrom ┆ start ┆ end ┆ depth │
# │ str   ┆ i64   ┆ i64 ┆ u32   │
# ╞═══════╪═══════╪═════╪═══════╡
# │ chr1  ┆ 0     ┆ 5   ┆ 1     │
# │ chr1  ┆ 5     ┆ 10  ┆ 2     │
# │ chr1  ┆ 10    ┆ 15  ┆ 1     │
# └───────┴───────┴─────┴───────┘

docs.title: expand
docs.text:
Expand intervals by subtracting amount from start and adding to end. Use start_amount/end_amount to control each side independently. Start is clamped to 0. Returns same schema as a.

a = pl.DataFrame({"chrom": ["chr1"], "start": [100], "end": [200]})

result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.expand(a, amount=50))
# start=50, end=250

result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.expand(a, start_amount=10, end_amount=50))
# start=90, end=250

docs.title: shift
docs.text:
Translate all intervals by amount bases. Positive = rightward, negative = leftward. Start is clamped to 0; interval width is preserved. Returns same schema as a.

result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.shift(a, amount=1000))

docs.title: flank
docs.text:
Generate flanking regions adjacent to each interval.

  • start=True (default): flank before — [interval.start - width, interval.start)
  • start=False: flank after — [interval.end, interval.end + width)
a = pl.DataFrame({"chrom": ["chr1"], "start": [100], "end": [200]})

upstream   = pl.from_arrow(intervals.flank(a, width=50))            # [50, 100)
downstream = pl.from_arrow(intervals.flank(a, width=50, start=False)) # [200, 250)

docs.title: set_width
docs.text:
Resize each interval to exactly width bases.

anchor Behaviour "start" (default) keep start, set end = start + width "end" keep end, set start = end - width "center" keep midpoint, expand equally both sides 
result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.set_width(a, width=100, anchor="center"))

docs.title: tile
docs.text:
Split each interval into fixed-size tiles of width bases. The last tile may be smaller. All non-interval columns are repeated for each tile.

a = pl.DataFrame({"chrom": ["chr1"], "start": [0], "end": [25], "name": ["region1"]})

result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.tile(a, width=10))
# start: 0, 10, 20  |  end: 10, 20, 25  |  name: region1, region1, region1

docs.title: disjoin
docs.text:
Split overlapping intervals into non-overlapping disjoint pieces. Every output interval spans a unique depth-homogeneous region. Returns only chrom/start/end.

result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.disjoin(a))

docs.title: intersect_ranges
docs.text:
Return regions covered by both a and b. Clips overlapping pairs to their intersection and merges the result. Returns only chrom/start/end.

result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.intersect_ranges(a, b))

docs.title: union_ranges
docs.text:
Return regions covered by a or b (positional union). Equivalent to merging the concatenation of both interval sets. Returns only chrom/start/end.

result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.union_ranges(a, b))

docs.title: setdiff_ranges
docs.text:
Return regions in a not covered by b. Clips a intervals around all overlapping b intervals. Returns only chrom/start/end.

result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.setdiff_ranges(a, b))

docs.title: sort_bedframe
docs.text:
Sort intervals by (chrom, start). With natural_chrom_order=True (default), chromosomes are sorted numerically by suffix (chr1 < chr2 < chr10), not lexicographically.

result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.sort_bedframe(a))
result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.sort_bedframe(a, natural_chrom_order=False))

docs.title: on_cols — grouping key
docs.text:
Most two-input functions (nearest, count_overlaps, cluster, merge, subtract, complement, coverage, expand, shift, flank, set_width, tile, disjoin) accept an on_cols parameter.

When set, operations are performed independently within each group defined by those columns — useful for per-sample or per-strand analysis:

# Count overlaps separately per sample
result = pl.from_arrow(
    intervals.count_overlaps(a, b, on_cols=["sample_id"])
)

docs.title: cluster(a, on_cols=None)
docs.text:
Assign a cluster_id to each interval. Overlapping or adjacent intervals on the same chromosome share the same cluster_id (UInt32, 0-based).

Returns all columns from a plus "cluster_id" UInt32.

docs.title: complement(a, chrom_sizes=None, on_cols=None)
docs.text:
Return the gaps between intervals on each chromosome.

If chrom_sizes is provided, also emits leading gaps [0, first_start) and trailing gaps [last_end, chrom_size). Returns chrom/start/end columns only.

docs.title: count_overlaps(a, b, on_cols=None)
docs.text:
For each row in a, count how many rows in b it overlaps.

Both inputs must have columns named "chrom"/"contig"/"chr", "start"/"pos", and "end"/"stop". Rename columns before calling if needed.

Returns a pyarrow.RecordBatch with all columns from a plus a "count" UInt32 column. One row per input a row; count=0 when no overlap.

docs.title: coverage(a, on_cols=None)
docs.text:
Compute per-base coverage depth as contiguous blocks.

Returns chrom/start/end/depth (UInt32) columns. Depth is the number of input intervals covering each position. Zero-depth regions are not emitted.

docs.title: disjoin(a, on_cols=None)
docs.text:
Split overlapping intervals into non-overlapping disjoint pieces.

Every output interval spans a unique depth-homogeneous region. Returns chrom/start/end columns only.

docs.title: expand(a, amount=0, start_amount=None, end_amount=None)
docs.text:
Expand intervals by subtracting from start and adding to end.

amount sets both sides; start_amount/end_amount override individually. Start is clamped to 1. Returns same schema as a.

docs.title: flank(a, width, start=True)
docs.text:
Generate flanking regions adjacent to each interval.

When start=True (default): flank before — [interval.start - width, interval.start). When start=False: flank after — [interval.end, interval.end + width). Start clamped to 1. Returns same schema as a with replaced start/end.

docs.title: intersect_ranges(a, b)
docs.text:
Return regions covered by both a and b.

Clips overlapping pairs to their intersection and merges the result. Returns chrom/start/end columns only.

docs.title: merge(a, on_cols=None)
docs.text:
Merge overlapping intervals into non-overlapping spans.

Returns a pyarrow.RecordBatch with chrom/start/end columns only. Extra metadata columns are dropped (same semantics as bedtools merge).

docs.title: nearest(query, target, on_cols=None)
docs.text:
For each row in query, find the nearest row in target on the same chromosome.

Both inputs must have columns named "chrom"/"contig"/"chr", "start"/"pos", and "end"/"stop". Rename columns before calling if needed.

Returns a pyarrow.RecordBatch with one row per query row: - all columns from query prefixed "a_" - nearest target columns prefixed "b_" (null if no same-chromosome target) - "distance" Int64: 0 if overlapping, gap in bases otherwise, null if no same-chromosome target exists.

When multiple target rows are equidistant, the one with the smaller row index is returned. Uses all available CPU cores (Rayon parallel).

docs.title: overlap(a, b, how='join')
docs.text:
Find overlapping intervals between a and b.

Both inputs must have columns named "chrom"/"contig"/"chr", "start"/"pos", and "end"/"stop". Rename columns before calling if needed:

  • PyArrow: batch.rename_columns({"seqname": "chrom", ...})
  • Polars: df.rename({"seqname": "chrom", ...})
  • Pandas: df.rename(columns={"seqname": "chrom", ...})

Condition: a.start < b.end and b.start < a.end (half-open intervals). Cross-chromosome pairs are never overlapping. Parallel via Rayon.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default how 'join' | 'semi'

"join" (default) — one row per overlapping pair; columns from both inputs prefixed "a_" and "b_" respectively (inner join semantics). If b contains duplicates that all overlap the same row in a, each produces a separate output row.

"semi" — rows from a that have at least one overlap in b, preserving the schema of a without duplication (filter semantics).

'join'

Returns:

Type Description RecordBatch

"join": columns from a prefixed "a_", columns from b prefixed "b_". "semi": same schema as a.

docs.title: set_width(a, width, anchor='start')
docs.text:
Resize each interval to width bases.

anchor controls which end is fixed: - "start" (default): keep start, set end = start + width - "end": keep end, set start = end - width - "center": keep midpoint, expand equally both sides Returns same schema as a.

docs.title: setdiff_ranges(a, b)
docs.text:
Return regions in a not covered by b.

Clips a intervals around all overlapping b intervals. Returns chrom/start/end columns only.

docs.title: shift(a, amount)
docs.text:
Translate all intervals by amount bases (positive = right, negative = left).

Start is clamped to 1; interval width is preserved when clamping occurs. Returns same schema as a.

docs.title: sort_bedframe(a, natural_chrom_order=True)
docs.text:
Sort intervals by (chrom, start).

When natural_chrom_order=True (default), chromosomes are sorted numerically by suffix (chr1 < chr2 < chr10), not lexicographically. Returns same schema as a.

docs.title: subtract(a, b, on_cols=None)
docs.text:
Return rows of a that have no overlap with any row in b.

Row-mode: entire a rows are kept or dropped; no interval clipping. Returns the same schema as a.

docs.title: tile(a, width)
docs.text:
Split each interval into fixed-size tiles of width bases.

The last tile may be smaller. All non-interval columns are repeated for each tile. Returns same schema as a.

docs.title: union_ranges(a, b)
docs.text:
Return regions covered by a or b (positional union).

Equivalent to merging the concatenation of both interval sets. Returns chrom/start/end columns only.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
SAM/BAM alignment flags bitset.

Class-level constants (e.g. Flags.UNMAPPED) hold the individual bit values. Use bitwise operators (&, |) to combine or test flags.

Examples:

>>> flags = sam.Flags(0x0003)
>>> flags.is_segmented()
True
>>> bool(flags & sam.Flags(sam.Flags.UNMAPPED))
False

docs.title: bits()
docs.text: Return the raw 16-bit integer value of the flags.

docs.title: is_duplicate()
docs.text: PCR or optical duplicate (0x0400).

docs.title: is_first_segment()
docs.text: This is the first segment in the template (0x0040).

docs.title: is_last_segment()
docs.text: This is the last segment in the template (0x0080).

docs.title: is_mate_reverse_complemented()
docs.text: Next segment sequence is reverse complemented (0x0020).

docs.title: is_mate_unmapped()
docs.text: Next segment in template is unmapped (0x0008).

docs.title: is_properly_segmented()
docs.text: All segments are properly aligned (0x0002).

docs.title: is_qc_fail()
docs.text: Read fails quality controls (0x0200).

docs.title: is_reverse_complemented()
docs.text: Sequence is reverse complemented (0x0010).

docs.title: is_secondary()
docs.text: Secondary alignment (0x0100).

docs.title: is_segmented()
docs.text: Read is part of a template with multiple segments (0x0001).

docs.title: is_supplementary()
docs.text: Supplementary alignment (0x0800).

docs.title: is_unmapped()
docs.text: Segment is unmapped (0x0004).

SAM/BAM header containing reference sequences and other metadata.

Examples:

docs.text:
Mapping quality score (MAPQ) in the range 0–254. Value 255 means unavailable.

Examples:

>>> mq.get()

docs.title: get()
docs.text: Return the raw MAPQ byte value (0–254).

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
Step-by-step guides for common bioinformatics workflows with ladle.

Tutorial Description Reading alignment files Iterate BAM/SAM records, export to DataFrame, query by region Reading variant files Parse VCF/BCF, export to DataFrame, indexed region queries Interval operations Overlap, nearest, coverage, and other genomic interval analyses

docs.title: Reading alignment files
docs.text: This tutorial covers reading BAM and SAM files with ladle — from simple record iteration to columnar batch export and indexed region queries.

docs.title: Sequential record iteration (BAM)
docs.text:
from ladle.io.bam import Reader

with Reader.from_path("sample.bam") as r:
    header = r.read_header()
    for record in r:
        name  = record.name()             # bytes | None
        flags = record.flags()
        start = record.alignment_start()  # core.Position | None
        seq   = record.sequence()         # bytes

        print(name, int(flags), int(start) if start else None)

docs.title: Checking flags
docs.text:
Flags is a bitset with convenience predicates:

flags = record.flags()

if flags.is_unmapped():
    continue
if flags.is_reverse_complemented():
    print("reverse strand")
if flags.is_duplicate():
    print("PCR duplicate")

# Raw bitwise access
is_primary = not (flags.is_secondary() or flags.is_supplementary())

docs.title: Export all records to a DataFrame
docs.text:
from ladle.io.bam import Reader

with Reader.from_path("sample.bam") as r:
    r.read_header()
    batch = r.records_to_batch()

# Pick your DataFrame library
df = batch.to_polars()
df = batch.to_arrow()
df = batch.to_pandas()

The batch contains these columns:

Column Type Description name LargeBinary Read name (QNAME) flags UInt16 SAM flags reference_sequence_id Int32 0-based ref seq index (null if unmapped) alignment_start Int32 1-based start (null if unmapped) mapping_quality UInt8 MAPQ (null if 255) cigar LargeBinary Raw CIGAR bytes mate_reference_sequence_id Int32 Mate ref seq index mate_alignment_start Int32 Mate 1-based start template_length Int32 TLEN sequence LargeBinary SEQ quality_scores LargeBinary Raw Phred QUAL bytes

docs.title: Iterate back from a batch
docs.text:
If you need to go back to record objects after loading the batch:

with Reader.from_path("sample.bam") as r:
    r.read_header()
    batch = r.records_to_batch()

for record in batch.to_iterator():
    print(record.name())

docs.title: Region query with a BAI index
docs.text:
Use IndexedReader to fetch only reads that overlap a genomic region. A .bai index file must exist next to the BAM file.

from ladle.io.bam import IndexedReader
from ladle.io.core import Region, Interval

with IndexedReader.from_path("sample.bam") as r:
    header = r.read_header()
    region = Region(b"chr1", Interval(1_000_000, 2_000_000))
    for record in r.query(header, region):
        print(record.name(), record.alignment_start())

Or parse the region from a string:

region = Region.parse("chr1:1000000-2000000")

docs.title: Reading SAM files
docs.text:
sam.Reader has the same interface as bam.Reader:

from ladle.io.sam import Reader

with Reader.from_path("sample.sam") as r:
    header = r.read_header()
    for record in r:
        print(record.name(), record.reference_sequence_name())

Note that SAM records use reference sequence name (bytes) rather than an integer ID.

docs.title: Writing BAM
docs.text:
from ladle.io.bam import Reader, Writer

with Reader.from_path("input.bam") as r:
    header = r.read_header()
    with Writer.from_path("output.bam") as w:
        w.write_header(header)
        for record in r:
            if not record.flags().is_unmapped():
                w.write_record(header, record)

docs.title: Interval operations
docs.text: This tutorial shows how to use ladle.ops.intervals for common genomic interval analyses. All functions accept PyArrow, Polars, or Pandas DataFrames and return a pyarrow.RecordBatch.

docs.title: Input requirements
docs.text:
Every DataFrame must have columns named chrom (or contig/chr), start, and end. Rename before calling if your schema differs:

df = df.rename({"seqname": "chrom", "chromStart": "start", "chromEnd": "end"})

docs.title: Overlap between two interval sets
docs.text:
A typical workflow: find all BAM reads overlapping variant sites.

import polars as pl
import ladle.ops.intervals as intervals
from ladle.io.bam import Reader as BamReader
from ladle.io.vcf import Reader as VcfReader

# Load BAM batch and create interval columns (0-based half-open)
with BamReader.from_path("sample.bam") as r:
    r.read_header()
    reads = (
        r.records_to_batch()
        .to_polars()
        .rename({"reference_sequence_id": "chrom"})
        .with_columns(end=pl.col("alignment_start") + pl.col("sequence").bin.count())
        .rename({"alignment_start": "start"})
    )

# Load VCF variants
with VcfReader.from_path("variants.vcf") as r:
    header = r.read_header()
    variants = (
        r.records_to_batch(header)
        .to_polars()
        .with_columns(
            start=pl.col("pos") - 1,
            end=pl.col("pos") - 1 + pl.col("ref").str.len_bytes(),
        )
        .rename({"chrom": "chrom"})
    )

result = pl.from_arrow(intervals.overlap(reads, variants))
print(f"{len(result)} read-variant overlaps found")

docs.title: Count how many variants fall in each read
docs.text:
counts = pl.from_arrow(intervals.count_overlaps(reads, variants))
print(counts.filter(pl.col("count") > 0).head())

docs.title: Find the nearest gene for each variant
docs.text:
genes = pl.read_csv("genes.bed", separator="\t",
                    new_columns=["chrom", "start", "end", "gene_name"])

nearest = pl.from_arrow(intervals.nearest(variants, genes))
# nearest contains a_* columns (variant) + b_* columns (nearest gene) + distance
print(nearest.select(["a_chrom", "a_start", "b_gene_name", "distance"]).head())

docs.title: Merge overlapping peaks
docs.text:
peaks = pl.read_csv("peaks.bed", separator="\t",
                    new_columns=["chrom", "start", "end", "score"])

merged = pl.from_arrow(intervals.merge(peaks))
print(f"Reduced {len(peaks)} peaks to {len(merged)} merged regions")

docs.title: Compute coverage from alignments
docs.text:
with BamReader.from_path("sample.bam") as r:
    r.read_header()
    reads = r.records_to_batch().to_polars()

# Build interval columns
reads = reads.with_columns(
    start=pl.col("alignment_start") - 1,
    end=pl.col("alignment_start") - 1 + pl.col("sequence").bin.count(),
    chrom=pl.col("reference_sequence_id").cast(pl.Utf8),
).filter(pl.col("start").is_not_null())

cov = pl.from_arrow(intervals.coverage(reads))
# chrom / start / end / depth
print(cov.filter(pl.col("depth") > 10).head())

blacklist = pl.read_csv("blacklist.bed", separator="\t",
                        new_columns=["chrom", "start", "end"])

clean_peaks = pl.from_arrow(intervals.subtract(peaks, blacklist))

docs.title: Per-sample analysis with on_cols
docs.text:
Use on_cols to run any operation independently within groups:

# peaks has a "sample" column
per_sample_merged = pl.from_arrow(
    intervals.merge(peaks, on_cols=["sample"])
)

docs.title: Reading variant files
docs.text: This tutorial covers reading VCF and BCF files — per-record iteration, header inspection, columnar batch export, and indexed region queries.

docs.title: Sequential record iteration (VCF)
docs.text:
from ladle.io.vcf import Reader

with Reader.from_path("variants.vcf") as r:
    header = r.read_header()
    for record in r:
        chrom = record.reference_sequence_name()  # str
        pos   = record.variant_start()            # core.Position | None
        ref   = record.reference_bases()          # str
        alts  = record.alternate_bases()          # list[str]
        qual  = record.quality_score()            # float | None
        print(chrom, int(pos) if pos else None, ref, alts, qual)

docs.title: Inspecting the header
docs.text:
with Reader.from_path("variants.vcf") as r:
    header = r.read_header()

print(header.sample_names())   # ['NA12878', 'NA12879']
print(header.contigs())        # {'chr1': 248956422, 'chr2': 242193529, ...}
print(header.info_fields())    # [('DP', 'Integer'), ('AF', 'Float'), ...]
print(header.format_fields())  # [('GT', 'String'), ('GQ', 'Integer'), ...]

docs.title: Reading INFO fields
docs.text:
with Reader.from_path("variants.vcf") as r:
    header = r.read_header()
    for record in r:
        info = record.info(header)
        dp = info.get("DP")   # int | None
        af = info.get("AF")   # float | None
        print(dp, af)

docs.title: Export all records to a DataFrame
docs.text:
from ladle.io.vcf import Reader

with Reader.from_path("variants.vcf") as r:
    header = r.read_header()
    batch  = r.records_to_batch(header)   # pass header to decode INFO columns

df = batch.to_polars()
print(df.head())

docs.title: Sequential record iteration (BCF)
docs.text:
BCF records need the header to resolve string maps:

from ladle.io.bcf import Reader

with Reader.from_path("variants.bcf") as r:
    header = r.read_header()
    for record in r:
        chrom = record.reference_sequence_name(header)  # requires header
        pos   = record.variant_start()
        ref   = record.reference_bases()                # bytes (BCF)
        alts  = record.alternate_bases()
        print(chrom, int(pos) if pos else None)

docs.title: Indexed region query (BCF)
docs.text:
bcf.IndexedReader uses a .csi index for random access:

from ladle.io.bcf import IndexedReader
from ladle.io.core import Region, Interval

with IndexedReader.from_path("variants.bcf") as r:
    header = r.read_header()
    region = Region.parse("chr1:1000000-2000000")
    for record in r.query(header, region):
        print(record.reference_sequence_name(header), record.variant_start())

docs.title: Writing VCF
docs.text:
from ladle.io.vcf import Reader, Writer

with Reader.from_path("input.vcf") as r:
    header = r.read_header()
    with Writer.from_path("output.vcf") as w:
        w.write_header(header)
        for record in r:
            if record.quality_score() is not None:
                w.write_record(header, record)

docs.title: Cross-format: VCF → BCF
docs.text:
from ladle.io.vcf import Reader
from ladle.io.bcf import Writer

with Reader.from_path("variants.vcf") as r:
    header = r.read_header()
    with Writer.from_path("variants.bcf") as w:
        w.write_header(header)
        for record in r:
            w.write_vcf_record(header, record)
